# LightClaw

> LightClaw is an alpha, self-hosted Telegram control surface for reviewed and verified work by local Codex and Claude coding agents. Telegram and configured hosted model providers remain external services. Workspaces and private run receipts stay local by default. The deterministic demo uses fixtures, costs zero, and does not prove live-provider quality. LightClaw never pushes or publishes a demo result.

Allowlisted bots accept commands only in private Telegram chats. Public groups require explicit public mode and no user allowlist. Conversation and memory are shared within each session. Only the requester can use plan, voice, or trusted-run controls, cancel active runs, or accept, reject, and retry results; all group members can view run diffs. Forum topic IDs create separate sessions.

Plan, voice, and trusted-run approvals expire even if the clock changes or the machine sleeps.

Text requests are limited to 20 per Telegram user per minute before model processing. Voice transcription is limited to six requests per user per minute and 20 MB per file. Rate limits are process-local and reset on restart.

Memory and job SQLite databases, including existing WAL/SHM sidecars, are restricted to owner-only permissions before use.

Telegram `/agent runs` lists up to ten durable jobs for the current chat, with status and a short goal preview; multi-agent jobs include lane-state counts, and completed runs have a **View diff** button. The SQLite session filter keeps other chats out of the list, and history actions remain available after bot restarts.

Chat history and session summaries live in namespaced local SQLite memory. They expire after 90 days by default; MEMORY_RETENTION_DAYS changes the limit. Telegram /clear removes the current chat or forum-topic session; global /wipe_memory erases saved chat memory across chats. A group confirmation lasts 90 seconds and must come from the initiating Telegram user.

Automatic edit retries omit common credential paths and file contents with detectable secrets. Model-generated file blocks refuse common credential paths; detection is heuristic.

Telegram replies and saved long-result artifacts redact configured secrets and recognizable credential patterns; detection is heuristic.

Delegated CLI output has per-line and per-stream limits. LightClaw marks truncated output for review.

Automatic task Git commands disable configured hooks and filesystem monitors; staging and checkouts bypass configured filters, commits skip signing, and diffs ignore external helpers.

Selective local artifact apply requires a confirmed SHA-256 plan bound to source and target contents and permissions. All selected sources are staged and verified before target backups begin. If backup preparation fails, backups created in that attempt are removed and no selected file is replaced. A new target that appears during apply is not overwritten.
